findings.message: The final-pass fix for reused GitHub logins only covers the connect path. It stores GitHub's id in `provider_user_id`, and `setGitHubIdentities` checks it when someone connects. Commit attribution never reads that column. `findGitIdentity` still matches a commit's author by login first. `authorOf` (modules/delivery/server/ingest.ts:41-43) then credits the row's person whenever GitHub verified the commit, without checking the account id. The case the earlier finding named is the one this misses: a person renames on GitHub and never reconnects, and someone else takes the old login. The fix only helps if the person reconnects. To fix it, stop crediting a commit by login alone when the matched row has a `provider_user_id`. Require the commit email to match that row's verified email, or compare the push's account id when the payload has one. Add a table test with at least three cases: a renamed login reused by another GitHub user with a signed commit, the same login still held by its original owner, and a row with no recorded id.
findings.scenario: Kasun connects as @kasun-dias (id 4821937), then renames on GitHub to @kd and doesn't reconnect. An outsider registers @kasun-dias and pushes a commit GitHub has verified (their own key, author username kasun-dias). `findGitIdentity` returns Kasun's row by login, `c.verified` is true, so `authorOf` returns Kasun's userId. The outsider's commit closes Kasun's tasks and drafts hours for Kasun.

findings.message: Final pass 2 made the 'connected' note come only from the stored record, but this fix covers just the login and email count. The 'N more are linked to another person; ask an Admin' sentence still comes straight from the URL's `skipped` value, with nothing checking it. The other result codes are also shown just because they appear in the URL. Anyone can build a /git-accounts link that tells a connected person their emails are taken by someone else, or that their link expired, and send them to an Admin. Fix: pass the skipped count and the failure reason through a server-side record keyed to the person's claim, for example columns on git_accounts.connect_state such as `skipped`/`result`, and read them back on the page. Alternatively, drop the URL-supplied count and failure codes when no recent claim of this viewer's matches them.
findings.scenario: A signed-in person with GitHub connected opens /git-accounts?github=connected&skipped=4 → the page says 'GitHub connected as @kasun-dias: 2 emails. 4 more are linked to another person; ask an Admin', though nothing was skipped. The same happens with ?github=login-taken, which shows 'that GitHub login is linked to another person' with no connect attempted.

findings.message: The `app.github-callback` slot is defined twice: in this route (its own `GitHubCallback` type and the string "app.github-callback") and in modules/git-accounts/server/callback.ts (`GITHUB_CALLBACK_SLOT` and the same type). Nothing checks that the two copies match. If the module renames the slot or changes the handler's shape, the build still passes, and the route silently returns 404 or calls the handler with the wrong arguments. Declare the slot's name and type once in a shared package (for example @amax/core), and have both the app and the module import it.
findings.scenario: The module changes the slot name to "app.github-return". Type-checking still passes, `provided()` returns [] in the route, and every GitHub return gets 'Not found'.

findings.message: This change adds a new kind of slot: one the app reads (`app.github-callback`), filled by a module's `provides`. The 'Module slots (081)' section of docs/architecture.md only describes slots that one module declares in its contracts.ts and another module fills. Add a line saying the app may also read a slot this way, where that slot's name and type live, and name this one.

When the session has lapsed while the person is on GitHub, the callback returns a bare 404. The connect state stays unclaimed but can't be finished, and the person sees no message. Redirect to sign-in with a return to the callback URL, or to /git-accounts with an 'incomplete' result, instead of a 404.
findings.scenario: A person's session expires while they are on GitHub's authorize page → GitHub sends them back to /api/git/github/callback?code=…&state=… → they get 'Not found' with no way to continue.
